q: In Belgium, what percentage of the total population lives in the Flemish region and speaks Dutch?
e: Of Belgium’s total population, 59% lives in the Flemish region and speaks Dutch, 40% lives in Wallonia speaking French, and 1% speaks German.

q: In Belgium’s capital city Brussels, 80% of the people speak which language?
e: In Brussels, 80% people speak French while 20% are Dutch-speaking.

q: In which year did Sri Lanka emerge as an independent country?
e: Sri Lanka emerged as an independent country in 1948.

q: Under the Act passed in Sri Lanka in 1956, which language was recognised as the only official language?
e: In 1956, an Act was passed to recognise Sinhala as the only official language, thus disregarding Tamil.

q: Approximately what percentage of Sri Lanka’s population consists of Sinhala-speakers?
e: In Sri Lanka, the major social groups are the Sinhala-speakers (74%) and the Tamil-speakers (18%).

q: How many times did Belgian leaders amend their constitution between 1970 and 1993?
e: Between 1970 and 1993, Belgium amended its constitution four times so as to work out an arrangement enabling everyone to live together.

q: When many countries of Europe came together to form the European Union, which city was chosen as its headquarters?
e: Brussels was chosen as the headquarters of the European Union.

q: What is the third kind of government in Belgium elected by people belonging to one language community, having power over cultural, educational and language issues?
e: Apart from Central and State governments, Belgium has a third kind of government called "community government" elected by one language community.

q: What is the sharing of power among different organs of government—legislature, executive and judiciary—called?
e: Power shared among different organs of government (legislature, executive, judiciary) at the same level is called horizontal distribution of power.

q: Which reason states that power sharing is the "very spirit of democracy"?
e: Moral reasons emphasise the very act of power sharing as valuable and as the very spirit of democracy.

q: Which reason stresses that power sharing helps reduce the possibility of conflict between social groups?
e: Prudential reasons stress that power sharing will bring out better outcomes, reducing social conflict and ensuring political stability.

q: By the 1980s in Sri Lanka, several political organisations were formed demanding an independent state called:
e: By 1980s several political organisations demanded an independent Tamil Eelam (state) in northern and eastern parts of Sri Lanka.

q: What is the division of power involving higher and lower levels of government (Union, State, Local) called?
e: Division of powers involving higher and lower levels of government is called vertical division of power.

q: Which arrangement in India exemplifies power sharing among different social groups?
e: The system of "reserved constituencies" in assemblies and parliament in India shares power among weaker social sections.

q: The Tamil natives of Sri Lanka (13% of total population) are called:
e: Among the 18% Tamils, Tamil natives of the country are called "Sri Lankan Tamils" (13%), while the rest (whose forefathers came from India as plantation workers) are "Indian Tamils".

q: What is the system of government in which power is divided between a central authority and various constituent units of the country called?
e: Federalism is a system of government in which power is divided between a central authority and various constituent units of the country.

q: How many languages in total are recognised as Scheduled Languages in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution (Hindi plus 21 others)?
e: Besides Hindi, there are 21 other languages recognised as Scheduled Languages by the Constitution, making 22 Scheduled Languages in total.

q: Under the Indian Constitution, defence, foreign affairs, banking, communications and currency belong to which list?
e: Union List includes subjects of national importance such as defence, foreign affairs, banking, communications and currency; the Union Government alone can make laws on them.

q: Police, trade, commerce, agriculture and irrigation are subjects included in which list of the Indian Constitution?
e: State List contains subjects of State and local importance such as police, trade, commerce, agriculture and irrigation.

q: Education, forest, trade unions, marriage, adoption and succession are subjects in which list?
e: Concurrent List includes subjects of common interest to both Union and State Governments, such as education, forest, trade unions, marriage, adoption and succession.

q: Who has the power to legislate on "residuary subjects" like computer software under the Indian Constitution?
e: The Union Government has the power to legislate on "residuary" subjects that do not fall in any of the three lists, such as computer software.

q: Under the 1992 decentralisation amendment in India, at least what fraction of all positions in local government bodies was reserved for women?
e: At least one-third of all positions in local government bodies are reserved for women under the 1992 amendment.

q: What is the political head of a Municipal Corporation called?
e: A municipal chairperson is the political head of a municipality; in a municipal corporation such an office-bearer is called the Mayor.

q: Under whose overall supervision does the Gram Panchayat work, comprising all the voters in the village?
e: The Gram Panchayat works under the overall supervision of the Gram Sabha; all the voters in the village are its members.

q: Which independent institution has been created in each State to conduct panchayat and municipal elections?
e: An independent institution called the State Election Commission has been created in each State to conduct panchayat and municipal elections.

q: Which of the following is an example of a "coming together" federation?
e: "Coming together" federations include the USA, Switzerland and Australia; India, Spain and Belgium are "holding together" federations.

q: How does the Indian Constitution declare India?
e: The Constitution declared India as a Union of States; although it did not use the word federation, the Indian Union is based on the principles of federalism.

q: Which states in India were created NOT on the basis of language, but to recognise differences based on culture, ethnicity or geography?
e: States like Nagaland, Uttarakhand and Jharkhand were created not on the basis of language but to recognise differences based on culture, ethnicity or geography.

q: What is the district-level institution of the rural Panchayati Raj system called?
e: A few gram panchayats are grouped together to form a panchayat samiti/block/mandal, and all panchayat samitis in a district together constitute the Zilla (district) Parishad.

q: Units of the Indian Union that are too small to become independent states and cannot be merged with existing states (like Chandigarh, Lakshadweep, Delhi) are called:
e: Areas like Chandigarh, Lakshadweep or the capital city of Delhi are called Union Territories, which do not have the powers of a State; the Central Government has special powers in running them.

q: Belgium shares its borders with which four European countries?
o: France, the Netherlands, Germany and Luxembourg
e: Belgium is a small country in Europe sharing borders with France, the Netherlands, Germany and Luxembourg.

q: How many languages are included in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution? [JAC PYQ]
e: There are 22 Scheduled Languages (Hindi plus 21 other languages) in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution.

q: Which one of the following subjects falls under the Concurrent List? [JAC PYQ]
e: Education and Forests are in the Concurrent List; Defence and Currency are in the Union List; Police is in the State List.

q: Which three lists distribute legislative powers between Union and State Governments under the Indian Constitution? [JAC Model 2026]
o: Union List, State List and Concurrent List
e: The Constitution clearly provides a three-fold distribution of legislative powers: Union List, State List and Concurrent List.

q: In which year was a major constitutional step taken towards real decentralisation in India, making local body elections mandatory?
e: A major step towards decentralisation was taken in 1992 when the Constitution was amended to make the third-tier of democracy more powerful and effective.

q: If laws made by the Union Government and a State Government on a Concurrent List subject conflict with each other, which law prevails?
o: Law made by the State Government
Law made by the Union Government
e: Both Union and State Governments can make laws on Concurrent List subjects; if their laws conflict with each other, the law made by the Union Government prevails.

q: In Brussels’ separate government under the Belgian accommodation model, what representation was given to Dutch and French-speaking people?
e: Brussels has a separate government in which both communities have equal representation; French-speaking people accepted equal representation in Brussels because Dutch-speaking people accepted equal representation in Central Government.

q: Why can the Union Parliament NOT unilaterally change the basic sharing of power between the Union Government and State Governments in India?
o: Any change requires passage by both Houses of Parliament with at least two-thirds majority and ratification by the legislatures of at least half of the total States
Because the Constitution can never be amended
Because only the President amends it
Because only the Supreme Court legislates
e: Parliament cannot on its own change this fundamental arrangement; any change has to be first passed by both Houses with at least two-thirds majority and then ratified by legislatures of at least half of total States.

q: Unlike Belgium’s accommodation, which approach did the democratically elected government in Sri Lanka adopt after 1948?
e: In Sri Lanka, the democratically elected government adopted a series of majoritarian measures to establish Sinhala supremacy.

q: What brought a major positive shift towards respecting State autonomy in Centre-State relations in India after 1990?
o: Rise of regional political parties in many states and the beginning of the era of Coalition Governments at the Centre
e: After 1990, the rise of regional parties and the era of coalition governments at the Centre fostered a new culture of power sharing and respect for autonomy of State Governments, backed by a Supreme Court judgement.

q: Which form of power sharing creates a "system of checks and balances" among institutions?
o: Horizontal distribution among Legislature, Executive and Judiciary
Vertical division between Centre and Panchayat
e: Under horizontal distribution, none of the organs exercises unlimited power; each organ checks the others, resulting in a balance of power called a system of checks and balances.

q: Why do states like Assam, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram enjoy special powers under Article 371 of the Indian Constitution?
o: Due to peculiar social and historical circumstances, especially for protection of land rights of indigenous peoples, culture and preferential employment
e: Under Article 371, these states enjoy special powers due to peculiar social and historical circumstances—protecting land rights of indigenous peoples, culture and preferential government employment.

q: The story of "Khalil’s dilemma" in NCERT illustrates power sharing between different religious communities in which country?
e: Khalil’s dilemma in Beirut illustrates Lebanon’s agreed power-sharing pact among religious sects (President Maronite Catholic, PM Sunni Muslim, Deputy PM Orthodox Christian, Speaker Shia Muslim).

q: In Germany (2005), how did the two historically rival parties—the Christian Democratic Union and the Social Democratic Party—share power?
o: By forming a Grand Coalition Government
e: Because neither got a clear majority in 2005, the two rival parties formed a grand coalition government.

q: Roughly how many of the world’s 193 countries have federal political systems, though their citizens make up about 40% of world population?
e: Though only 25 of the world’s 193 countries have federal political systems, their citizens make up 40 per cent of the world’s population.

q: Under India’s language policy, what constitutional status is given to Hindi?
e: Our Constitution did not give the status of national language to any one language; Hindi was identified as the official language alongside 21 other Scheduled Languages.

q: When the use of English for official purposes was scheduled to stop in 1965, violent protests took place in which state leading the Central Government to continue English alongside Hindi?
e: Many non-Hindi speaking States demanded that the use of English continue; in Tamil Nadu, this movement took a violent form, so the Central Government agreed to continue English along with Hindi.

q: Approximately how many elected representatives sit in panchayats and municipalities across India today?
e: Now there are about 36 lakh elected representatives in the panchayats and municipalities all over the country—making it the largest experiment in democracy anywhere in the world.

q: Which Brazilian city carried out an extraordinary experiment in combining decentralisation with participative democracy for preparing its municipal budget?
e: The city of Porto Alegre in Brazil combined decentralisation with participative democracy, where nearly 20,000 local inhabitants participate in deciding the city’s budget.

q: What was the major weakness of local governments (panchayats and municipalities) in India prior to the 1992 constitutional amendment?
o: Elections were not held regularly and local bodies did not have any powers or resources of their own
They prepared the national Union budget
e: Before 1992, local bodies were directly under State Government control, elections were not held regularly, and they had no powers or resources of their own.

q: Which level of government holds exclusive authority over India’s nuclear/defence tests (such as Pokhran in Rajasthan) and foreign policy? [JAC 2026 context]
e: Defence, atomic energy and foreign affairs are in the Union List, meaning only the Union Government can take decisions like nuclear testing in Pokhran (Rajasthan).

q: In which system of government are sub-units subordinate to the central government, allowing the central government to pass on orders to provincial/local governments?
e: Under the unitary system, sub-units are subordinate to the central government which can pass orders to provincial/local governments; in a federal system, the central government cannot order the state government to do something.

q: What crucial constitutional role do Courts (especially the Supreme Court) play in Indian federalism?
o: Acting as an umpire by interpreting the Constitution and the powers of different levels of government in case of disputes
e: Courts have the power to interpret the Constitution and powers of different levels; the highest court acts as an umpire if disputes arise between different levels of government.

q: How do interest groups—such as those of traders, businessmen, industrialists, farmers and industrial workers—participate in power sharing?
o: Through participation in governmental committees or bringing influence on the decision-making process
e: Interest groups like traders, businessmen, industrialists, farmers and workers also have a share in governmental power through participation in committees or influencing decision-making.

q: Why did some national leaders initially fear creating linguistic states in India, and what did experience actually prove?
o: They feared it would lead to disintegration of the country, but experience showed formation of linguistic states actually made the country more united and administration easier
e: Leaders feared disintegration, yet experience showed that the formation of linguistic states has actually made the country more united and made administration easier.

q: Under the new constitutional stipulations following Sri Lanka’s 1956 majoritarian policies, which religion was the state bound to protect and foster?
e: A new constitution stipulated that the state shall protect and foster Buddhism.

q: Before 1990, what frequent misuse by the Central Government undermined the spirit of federalism in India when rival parties ruled States?
o: Central Government often misused the Constitution to dismiss State governments controlled by rival parties
e: Before 1990, when the Centre and States had different ruling parties, the Centre tried to undermine State power and often misused the Constitution to dismiss rival State governments.

q: What does "jurisdiction" mean in a federal system?
o: The area over which someone has legal authority, defined in terms of geographical boundaries or certain subjects
e: Jurisdiction: The area over which someone has legal authority, defined in terms of geographical boundaries or in terms of certain subjects.

q: At least how many times in a year has the Gram Sabha to meet to approve the annual budget of the Gram Panchayat and review its performance?
o: At least twice or thrice in a year
e: The Gram Sabha has to meet at least twice or thrice in a year to approve the annual budget of the gram panchayat and to review its performance.

q: How is financial autonomy ensured for each tier of government in a federal system?
o: Sources of revenue for each level of government are clearly specified to ensure its financial autonomy
States depend purely on foreign charity
e: Sources of revenue for each level of government are clearly specified to ensure its financial autonomy.

q:
Match the four forms of power sharing with their appropriate examples:
A. Horizontal distribution — 1. Union, State and Local governments
B. Vertical division — 2. Community govt in Belgium / Reserved constituencies in India
C. Among social groups — 3. Legislature, Executive and Judiciary
D. Political parties & pressure groups — 4. Coalition govts and farmer/trader interest groups
e: Horizontal = Organs (A-3); Vertical = Tiers (B-1); Social groups = Community govt/reserved seats (C-2); Parties/groups = Coalitions/interest groups (D-4).

q: If a ruling group denies equal linguistic and job opportunities to another community in order to dominate the state, which model does this resemble and what outcome does NCERT warn of?
o: It resembles Sri Lanka’s majoritarianism, which alienates communities and undermines national unity, risking civil strife
e: When one community imposes its will disregarding others (majoritarianism as in Sri Lanka), it fosters alienation, weakens national unity and risks violent conflict.

q: Subjects like computer software and e-commerce came up after the Constitution was written. Who can legislate on them and under which power?
o: The Union Government, under its "residuary" legislative powers
Only State Governments under State List
No legislature can pass laws on them
e: Under the Indian Constitution, any subject not falling in the three lists—including post-1950 subjects like computer software—is a residuary subject under Union legislative authority.

q: If a State Legislature passes a law on "Adoption" (Concurrent List) and the Union Parliament passes a conflicting law on Adoption, which will prevail?
o: The law made by the Union Parliament
The law made by the State Legislature
The Supreme Court drafts a replacement
e: On Concurrent List subjects, if State and Union laws conflict with each other, the law made by the Union Government prevails.

q: How does the distribution of power between Centre and States differ in "coming together" (USA, Australia) versus "holding together" (India, Spain) federations?
o: In "coming together" federations all constituent states usually have equal power and are strong vis-a-vis the federal govt, while in "holding together" federations the central govt tends to be more powerful and units may have unequal powers
In USA states have zero power
e: Coming together (USA, Switzerland, Australia) gives states equal and strong power vis-a-vis federal govt; holding together (India, Spain, Belgium) makes Central Govt stronger, often with unequal/special powers.

q: Even though India’s Central Government holds strong powers, what constitutional safeguard guarantees that India remains truly Federal rather than Unitary?
o: Legislative powers are constitutionally divided across three lists, Parliament cannot unilaterally alter this power-sharing, revenue sources are specified and the Supreme Court acts as independent umpire
e: Constitutional division of powers, rigid amendment procedure requiring at least half the States’ ratification, specified revenue sources and an independent Supreme Court uphold federalism.

q:
Arrange the following political milestones chronologically (earliest to latest):
1. Independence of Sri Lanka
2. Major constitutional amendment for decentralisation in India
3. "Sinhala Only" official language Act in Sri Lanka
4. Beginning of Coalition era at the Centre reshaping Indian Centre-State relations
e: Sri Lanka Independence (1948) → Sinhala Only Act (1956) → Coalition era in India (1990) → Decentralisation amendment (1992).

q: Why was the ethnic distribution in Brussels considered an acute problem compared to the rest of Belgium?
o: Dutch-speaking people constituted a majority (59%) in the country, but a minority (20%) in the capital Brussels where French-speakers were 80%
e: The Dutch-speaking community constituted a majority in the country (59%), but a minority in the capital Brussels (20% vs 80% French).

q: Arrange the three levels of rural local government (Panchayati Raj) from lowest (village) to highest (district):
o: Gram Panchayat → Panchayat Samiti (Block/Mandal) → Zilla Parishad
Zilla Parishad → Gram Panchayat → Panchayat Samiti
Panchayat Samiti → Zilla Parishad → Gram Sabha
Municipal Corporation → Gram Panchayat → Zilla Parishad
e: Rural local self-government flows upward: Gram Panchayat (village/group of villages) → Panchayat Samiti/Block/Mandal → Zilla Parishad (district).

q: Why was a third tier of government (decentralisation) considered necessary inside large Indian states like UP and Maharashtra?
o: Many Indian states are as large as independent European nations and internally diverse, and large numbers of local problems/issues are best settled at the local level
e: Because states like UP and Maharashtra are huge and internally diverse, local people have better knowledge of local problems, spend money efficiently, and participate directly in decisions.

q: When two or more political parties form an alliance to contest elections and form a coalition government, which form of power sharing is seen?
o: Power sharing among political parties (indirect/direct via alliance and coalition)
e: When two or more parties form an alliance to contest elections and form a coalition government if elected, they share power directly.

q: Contrast India’s language policy with Sri Lanka’s post-1956 language approach:
o: India avoided imposing Hindi, recognised 22 Scheduled Languages and continued English with caution; Sri Lanka imposed Sinhala as the sole official language disregarding Tamil
e: Unlike Sri Lankan leaders who imposed Sinhala exclusively, Indian leaders showed flexibility, recognised 22 Scheduled Languages, and avoided forcing Hindi on non-Hindi states.

q: In India’s federal structure, a citizen residing in Mumbai is simultaneously governed by which tiers of government?
o: Union Government of India, State Government of Maharashtra, and Mumbai Municipal Corporation (local tier)
e: Different tiers of government govern the same citizens: Union Government, Maharashtra State Government, and the Municipal Corporation.

q: What are the "dual objectives" of a federal system as highlighted in NCERT?
o: To safeguard and promote unity of the country, while at the same time accommodate regional diversity
e: The federal system has dual objectives: to safeguard and promote unity of the country, while at the same time accommodate regional diversity (requiring mutual trust and agreement to live together).

q: Who elects Belgium’s "Community Government"?
o: People belonging to one language community (Dutch, French and German-speaking)—no matter where they live
e: "Community government" is elected by people belonging to one language community—Dutch, French and German-speaking—no matter where they live.

q: What social-democratic milestone did mandatory reservations for SC, ST, OBC and one-third women in local bodies (1992) achieve?
o: It ensured inclusive representation, deepened democracy, and increased women’s representation and voice in local decision-making
It restricted Sarpanch posts to landlords
e: Constitutional status for local government helped deepen democracy and increased women’s representation and voice alongside marginalised castes.

q: Despite 36 lakh elected representatives, what major challenge still limits the effectiveness of Panchayati Raj in India?
o: While elections are held regularly, Gram Sabhas are not held regularly, and most state governments have not transferred significant powers nor given adequate resources to local bodies
e: Per NCERT, elections are held regularly, yet Gram Sabhas are not held regularly, and most state governments have not transferred significant powers or given adequate resources to local governments.

q: Under Belgium’s amended constitutional model, when can a "special law" be passed in the Central Government?
o: Only when it has the support of a majority of members from each linguistic group
By the Prime Minister’s sole decree
e: Special laws require the support of the majority of members from each linguistic group, so no single community can make decisions unilaterally.

q: What crucial lesson does the tragic civil war in Sri Lanka teach about power sharing?
o: If a majority community wants to force its dominance over others and refuses to share power, it can undermine the unity of the country
Minority languages should always be suppressed
Power must be concentrated in one person
e: Sri Lanka reminds us that if a majority community wants to force its dominance over others and refuses to share power, it can undermine the unity of the country.

q: Who are members of a Zilla Parishad besides the elected members?
o: Members of the Lok Sabha and MLAs of that district and some other officials of other district level bodies
e: Most members of Zilla Parishad are elected; Members of the Lok Sabha and MLAs of that district and some officials of other district level bodies are also its members.

q: "Even though ministers and government officials exercise power, they are responsible to Parliament/Assemblies; similarly, judges appointed by executive can check functioning of executive or laws by legislatures." This defines:
o: System of checks and balances (Horizontal power sharing)
e: This exemplifies horizontal power sharing where different organs check each other, creating a system of checks and balances.

q: Which landmark Supreme Court intervention alongside coalition politics after 1990 strengthened federalism in India?
o: A major judgement of the Supreme Court that made it difficult for the Central Government to dismiss state governments in an arbitrary manner
e: Coalition politics was supported by a major judgement of the Supreme Court that made it difficult for the Central Government to dismiss state governments in an arbitrary manner.

q: Identify the option that correctly lists one subject each from Union List, State List, and Concurrent List (in that exact order):
e: Banking = Union List; Police = State List; Education = Concurrent List.

q: How are state-level official languages and Union recruitment examinations handled under India’s language policy?
o: States have their own official languages where most government work occurs, and candidates for Central Government examinations may opt to take exams in any Scheduled Language
Only Hindi is allowed in Central exams
e: States have their own official languages, candidates for Central Government exams can take tests in any Scheduled language, and English continues alongside Hindi.

q: How does a "prudential" reason differ from a "moral" reason for power sharing?
o: Prudential reasons stress better practical outcomes (stability, reducing conflict), whereas moral reasons emphasise the very act of power sharing as intrinsically valuable and democratic
e: Prudential reasons stress that power sharing brings out better outcomes (conflict reduction, stability); moral reasons emphasise the very act of power sharing as valuable in itself.

q: How does Belgium’s shift in 1993 compare with Sri Lanka’s unitary setup regarding provincial autonomy?
o: Belgium shifted from a unitary to a federal system giving constitutional powers to regional governments, while Sri Lanka practically remains a unitary system with powers centred in the national government
e: In 1993 Belgium shifted from a unitary to a federal form of government by granting constitutional powers to regional governments no longer dependent on the Central Govt; Sri Lanka continued as a unitary system.

q: According to NCERT’s key features of federalism, can the Central Government order a State Government to do something against its constitutional jurisdiction?
o: No, in a federal system the Central Government cannot order the state government to do something; state government has powers of its own for which it is not answerable to the central government
Yes, Centre can dismiss ministers anytime without law
e: In a federal system, the central government cannot order the state government to do something; state government has powers of its own and both are separately answerable to the people.

q: What tangible impact did Porto Alegre’s participative budgeting experiment bring to poor colonies?
o: The number of buses running to poor colonies increased and builders could not evict slum-dwellers without resettling them
e: In Porto Alegre, people decided real allocations ensuring more buses ran to poor colonies and builders could not evict slum-dwellers without resettlement; a similar experiment took place in some areas in Kerala.

q: Who elects the members of a Panchayat Samiti (block or mandal)?
o: All the panchayat members in that area
e: A few gram panchayats are grouped together to form a panchayat samiti (block/mandal); the members of this representative body are elected by all the panchayat members in that area.

q: Who directly elects the ward members (panch) and the president (sarpanch) of a Gram Panchayat?
o: Directly by all the adult population living in that ward or village
e: A Gram Panchayat is a council consisting of several ward members (panch) and a president (sarpanch), directly elected by all the adult population living in that ward or village.

q:
Assertion (A): Belgium successfully avoided civic strife and partition despite deep linguistic divisions.
Reason (R): Belgian leaders recognised regional differences and cultural diversities, amending their constitution four times between 1970 and 1993 to craft an inclusive power-sharing model.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Both statements are true and Reason (R) accurately explains how Belgium’s 1970–1993 constitutional accommodation prevented division.

q:
Assertion (A): Majoritarian measures in Sri Lanka increased alienation among Sri Lankan Tamils and eventually triggered a civil war.
Reason (R): The 1956 Act recognised Sinhala as the sole official language, and preferential policies favoured Sinhala applicants for university positions and government jobs.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: The 1956 Sinhala Only Act and preferential policies directly explain the alienation and civil war in Sri Lanka.

q:
Assertion (A): Moral reasons for power sharing are based purely on a careful calculation of gains and losses to prevent political instability.
Reason (R): Actually, stressing better practical outcomes via calculation of gains and losses is a "prudential" reason, whereas "moral" reasons emphasise power sharing as the very spirit of democracy.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Assertion (A) is false because outcome-based calculation defines prudential reasons; Reason (R) is true.

q:
Assertion (A): India is an example of a "holding together" federation.
Reason (R): In India, the Central Government tends to be more powerful vis-a-vis the States, and some constituent units enjoy special powers under provisions like Article 371.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Greater strength of the Central Government and unequal/special powers of units characterise a holding together federation; R explains A.

q:
Assertion (A): If a Union law and a State law conflict on a Concurrent List subject, the State law prevails.
Reason (R): The Concurrent List includes subjects of common interest like education, forest, trade unions, marriage, adoption and succession.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Assertion (A) is false because the **Union Government’s** law prevails in case of conflict; Reason (R) is true.

q:
Assertion (A): Brussels has a separate government in which both Dutch and French-speaking communities have equal representation.
Reason (R): Brussels was chosen as the headquarters of the European Union.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Both statements are true facts, yet EU headquarters status did not cause equal representation in Brussels (it came from mutual accommodation with the Central Govt pact).

q:
Assertion (A): The Union Government has the authority to make laws on subjects like computer software that came up after the Constitution was framed.
Reason (R): Under the Indian Constitution, the power to legislate on "residuary subjects" vests with the Union Government.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Since residuary powers vest with the Union Government under the Constitution, it legislates on new subjects like computer software.

q:
Assertion (A): Power sharing among Legislature, Executive and Judiciary is called horizontal distribution of power.
Reason (R): It allows different organs of government placed at the same level to exercise different powers, ensuring none exercises unlimited power and creating checks and balances.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

q:
Assertion (A): The Indian Constitution gave the status of National Language to Hindi.
Reason (R): Besides Hindi, there are 21 other languages recognised as Scheduled Languages by the Constitution.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Assertion (A) is false because the Constitution did NOT give national language status to any language (Hindi is Official Language); Reason (R) is true.

q:
Assertion (A): Federal power sharing in India has become more effective since 1990 than in the early decades.
Reason (R): Rise of regional parties led to coalition governments at the Centre, and a Supreme Court judgement made arbitrary dismissal of state governments difficult.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Both statements are true and Reason (R) correctly explains why federalism strengthened after 1990.

q:
Assertion (A): After the 1992 constitutional amendment, it became constitutionally mandatory to hold regular elections to local government bodies.
Reason (R): Today there are about 36 lakh elected representatives in panchayats and municipalities across India.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Both statements are true facts, yet 36 lakh elected representatives is a consequence of the 1992 amendment, not its cause.

q:

Reason (R): Here independent States come together on their own to form a bigger unit by pooling sovereignty and retaining identity, where all constituent States usually have equal power.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Both statements are true and Reason (R) defines and explains coming together federations accurately.

q:
Assertion (A): The Indian Parliament can unilaterally alter the power-sharing arrangement between the Union and States by a simple majority.
Reason (R): Any change to federal power-sharing must pass both Houses of Parliament with at least a two-thirds majority and be ratified by legislatures of at least half the total States.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) states the true constitutional requirement.

q:
Assertion (A): Formation of linguistic states in India actually made the country more united and administration easier.
Reason (R): Initially some national leaders feared that creating states on linguistic lines would lead to the disintegration of the country.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Both statements are historically true, yet the initial fear did not cause unity—practical experience proved those fears wrong.

q:
Assertion (A): The Gram Sabha approves the annual budget and reviews the performance of the Gram Panchayat.
Reason (R): Only government officers and the Sarpanch are members of the Gram Sabha.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Assertion (A) is true, while Reason (R) is false because ALL voters in the village are members of the Gram Sabha.

q:
Assertion (A): Defence, banking, currency and foreign affairs are included in the Union List.
Reason (R): The country needs a uniform policy on these matters of national importance throughout India, so only the Union Government can make laws on them.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: The need for uniform national policy across the country explains why these subjects belong exclusively to the Union List.

q:
Assertion (A): Coalition governments and organised interest/pressure groups are vital forms of power sharing in democracies.
Reason (R): Alliances share power directly among competing parties, while traders, farmers and workers influence government decisions through committees or pressure.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Both statements are true and Reason (R) explains how coalitions and interest groups ensure power does not remain in one hand.

q:

o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

e: Both statements are true (R highlights the overall positive consequence of India’s cautious flexibility rather than the immediate protest trigger).

Reason (R): These areas are too small to become independent states yet could not be merged with existing states, so the Central Government has special powers in running them.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Reason (R): Most state governments have actually not transferred significant powers to local bodies nor given them adequate resources, and Gram Sabhas often lack regular meetings.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

q:
Read the passage: "Two different sets of reasons can be given in favour of power sharing. Firstly, power sharing is good because it helps to reduce the possibility of conflict between social groups. Since social conflict often leads to violence and political instability, power sharing is a good way to ensure the stability of political order. Imposing the will of majority community over others may look like an attractive option in the short run, but in the long run it undermines the unity of the nation. The second, deeper reason why power sharing is good for democracies: Power sharing is the very spirit of democracy."

How does power sharing ensure stability of the political order?
o: By reducing the possibility of conflict between social groups, which often leads to violence and political instability
e: As stated in the passage, power sharing reduces conflict between social groups, avoiding violence and political instability.

q: What are the two categories of reasons described in the passage above?
e: The first set of reasons is called "prudential" and the second is called "moral".

q: According to the passage, what is the long-run outcome of imposing the will of the majority community over others?
o: It undermines the unity of the nation in the long run
e: While imposing majority will may seem attractive in the short run, in the long run it undermines the unity of the nation.

q: According to NCERT, tyranny of the majority is not just oppressive for the minority—what does it often do to the majority as well?
o: It often brings ruin to the majority as well
e: NCERT notes: "Tyranny of the majority is not just oppressive for the minority; it often brings ruin to the majority as well."

q: In a democracy, what defines a "legitimate government"?
o: One where citizens, through participation, acquire a stake in the system and have a right to be consulted on how they are governed
e: People have a right to be consulted on how they are to be governed; a legitimate government is one where citizens, through participation, acquire a stake in the system.

q:
Read the passage: "When power is taken away from Central and State governments and given to local government, it is called decentralisation. The basic idea behind decentralisation is that there are a large number of problems and issues which are best settled at the local level. People have better knowledge of problems in their localities. They also have better ideas on where to spend money and how to manage things more efficiently. Besides, at the local level it is possible for the people to directly participate in decision making."

What is meant by "decentralisation" of power?
o: Taking power away from Central and State governments and giving it to local government
Concentrating all power in the Union
Giving all power solely to States
e: Decentralisation occurs when power is taken away from Central and State governments and given to local government.

q: Why can many issues and problems be settled best at the local level?
o: Because local people have better knowledge of problems in their localities, where to spend money, and how to manage things efficiently
Because rural citizens have no work
e: People have better knowledge of problems in their localities and better ideas on where to spend money and manage efficiently.

q: How does local government help realise the important principle of democracy—self-government?
o: It makes it possible for people to directly participate in decision making, inculcating a habit of democratic participation
e: At the local level, people directly participate in decision making, inculcating a habit of democratic participation.

q: Which provision was made constitutionally mandatory under the 1992 decentralisation amendment in India?
o: Regular elections to local government bodies and reservation of at least one-third of all positions for women
e: The 1992 amendment made regular elections mandatory, reserved seats for SC/ST/OBC, reserved at least 1/3rd seats for women, and created State Election Commissions.

q: What is rural local government popularly known as in India?
e: Rural local government is popularly known by the name Panchayati Raj.

q:
Evaluate the following demographic statements:
I. In Belgium’s capital Brussels, 80% speak Dutch and 20% speak French.
II. Across Belgium as a whole, 59% live in the Flemish region and speak Dutch.
III. In Sri Lanka, 74% are Sinhala-speakers and 18% are Tamil-speakers.
Which statements are correct?
e: Statements II and III are true. Statement I is false because in Brussels **80% speak French** and **20% speak Dutch**.

q: Which of the following list–subject pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
e: Police and trade belong to the State List, whereas residuary subjects cover matters not in any list (e.g., computer software).

q: Identify the INCORRECT statement regarding the Belgian model of accommodation:
o: Number of Dutch and French-speaking ministers shall be equal in Central Govt
Many Central Govt powers were given to State Govts of the two regions, not subordinate to Centre
Brussels has a separate government giving 80% representation to French and 20% to Dutch
Community government has power regarding cultural, educational and language issues
e: Brussels has a separate government in which both communities have **equal representation**, NOT an 80–20 split.

q:
Match the designated power-sharing offices in Lebanon (from Khalil’s dilemma in NCERT) with their communities:
A. President — 1. Shia Muslim
B. Prime Minister — 2. Orthodox Christian
C. Deputy Prime Minister — 3. Sunni Muslim
D. Speaker — 4. Maronite Catholic
e: In Lebanon’s post-civil-war power-sharing agreement: President = Maronite Catholic (A-4); PM = Sunni Muslim (B-3); Deputy PM = Orthodox Christian (C-2); Speaker = Shia Muslim (D-1).

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the key features of Federalism listed in NCERT?
o: There are two or more levels (tiers) of government
Different tiers govern the same citizens, each having its own jurisdiction in legislation, taxation and administration
Fundamental provisions of the constitution cannot be unilaterally changed by one level of government
If disputes arise between levels of government, the Prime Minister serves as the final constitutional umpire
e: The **highest court (Supreme Court)** acts as an umpire if disputes arise between different levels of government—not the Prime Minister.

q: Which statement regarding India’s Linguistic diversity and Language Policy in NCERT is INCORRECT?
o: 2011 Census recorded over 1,300 distinct mother tongues grouped into 121 major languages
Out of those, 22 are placed in the Eighth Schedule as Scheduled Languages
Even the largest language, Hindi, is the mother tongue of only about 43.63% of Indians
All 22 Scheduled Languages are spoken exclusively inside Uttar Pradesh
e: India’s 22 Scheduled Languages span diverse regions across the entire country, not a single state.

q:
Identify the power-sharing forms shown in three situations:
1. A farmers’ union lobbies the Agriculture Ministry committee on crop prices.
2. State govt frames its own agricultural policy while Union sets defence policy.
3. Two parties share ministerial berths in a coalition cabinet.
Which mapping is right?
o: 1: Interest/pressure groups; 2: Vertical (federal) division; 3: Power sharing among political parties
e: Farmers’ union lobbying = interest groups (1); State vs Union jurisdiction = vertical federal division (2); Coalition cabinet = political parties (3).

q: Suppose a futuristic subject like "Space Tourism and Satellite AI Law" arises and both a State Legislature and Parliament try to legislate on it. How does the Indian Constitution resolve jurisdiction here?
o: Since it is not listed in any of the three lists, it falls under Residuary Subjects where only the Union Parliament has legislative power
It automatically enters the State List
e: Subjects not mentioned in any of the three lists fall under residuary subjects on which the Union Government alone has the power to legislate.

q: Which item does NOT belong among the 1992 Constitutional Amendment provisions for decentralisation in India?
o: Constitutionally mandatory to hold regular elections to local bodies
Seats reserved for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes
At least one-third of all positions reserved for women
Local elections are conducted by a private committee appointed by the Prime Minister
e: An independent **State Election Commission** created in each State conducts panchayat and municipal elections.

q: Choose the option that cleanly separates three "Coming Together" countries from three "Holding Together" countries:
o: Coming together: USA, Switzerland, Australia; Holding together: India, Spain, Belgium
Coming together: India, Spain, Australia; Holding together: USA, Belgium, Switzerland
Both are China and Sri Lanka
e: Per NCERT: Coming together = USA, Switzerland and Australia; Holding together = India, Spain and Belgium.

q: How did the 1965 language transition controversy prove the wisdom of India’s leaders compared to Sri Lanka?
o: When non-Hindi states (especially Tamil Nadu) protested stopping English in 1965, the Central Govt wisely agreed to continue English along with Hindi rather than imposing uniformity
e: Rather than forcing uniformity like Sri Lanka, the Union Government showed flexibility and continued English alongside Hindi for official purposes while promoting Hindi without imposing it.

q: In Belgium’s constitutional arrangement, why did French-speaking people accept equal representation in Brussels even though they formed 80% of the capital?
o: Because the Dutch-speaking community (despite 59% national majority) had accepted equal representation in the Central Government
e: French-speaking people accepted equal representation in Brussels because the Dutch-speaking community accepted equal representation in the Central Government.

q: Among these four Indian states, which trio was created to recognise culture, ethnicity or geography rather than purely language?
e: NCERT explicitly names Nagaland, Uttarakhand and Jharkhand as states created to recognise differences based on culture, ethnicity or geography rather than language.

q: Are State Governments in India mere administrative agents of the Central Government?
o: No, State Governments derive independent legislative and revenue powers (State/Concurrent Lists) directly from the Constitution, which Parliament cannot unilaterally alter
Yes, Centre alters State Lists weekly
States lack authority over police or agriculture
e: Indian states possess constitutionally guaranteed jurisdiction over State List and Concurrent List subjects that cannot be changed unilaterally by Parliament.

q:
Match the local body with its political head:
1. Municipality (Towns) — A. Mayor
2. Municipal Corporation (Big Cities) — B. Sarpanch
3. Gram Panchayat — C. Municipal Chairperson
e: Municipality = Municipal Chairperson (1-C); Municipal Corporation = Mayor (2-A); Gram Panchayat = Sarpanch (3-B).

q: Which two cross-national examples are cited in NCERT to illustrate power sharing among different social groups?
o: "Community government" in Belgium and "Reserved constituencies" in assemblies/parliament in India
Tsardom in Russia and One-party in China
US Senate and House of Lords
Monarchy in Nepal and Sinhala Act in SL
e: "Community government" in Belgium is a good example, and India’s system of "reserved constituencies" in assemblies and parliament serves the same goal of giving minority/weaker social groups a fair share.

q: How does Lebanon’s power-sharing formula contrast with Sri Lanka’s post-1948 approach?
o: Lebanon ended civil war by distributing top executive/legislative posts across religious communities, whereas Sri Lanka triggered civil war by imposing Sinhala majority dominance
e: Lebanon’s leaders agreed on strict power-sharing rules across sects to preserve peace, whereas Sri Lanka’s refusal to share power sparked a devastating civil war.

q: Examine the true status of Indian languages under the 2011 Census and Eighth Schedule:
o: The 22 Scheduled Languages cover diverse states and a candidate in Central Govt examinations may opt to take the exam in any of these languages; Hindi is not imposed
Exams can only be written in Hindi
e: Candidates for Central Govt positions may take examinations in any of the 22 Scheduled Languages; the Eighth Schedule protects India’s rich linguistic diversity.

q: A village Sarpanch prepares and passes the Gram Panchayat’s annual budget entirely without calling any village meeting. Which institution’s mandatory authority has been bypassed?
o: Gram Sabha, which must meet at least twice or thrice a year to approve the annual budget and review performance
e: Gram Panchayat works under overall supervision of the Gram Sabha, which meets at least 2–3 times a year to approve the annual budget and review performance.

q: Which statement comparing the Union List and State List in India is INCORRECT?
o: Union List includes defence, foreign affairs, banking, communications and currency
State List includes police, trade, commerce, agriculture and irrigation
Only the Union Government alone can legislate on State List subjects
Subjects of common interest (education, forest) sit in Concurrent List
e: On subjects in the State List, **State Governments alone** can make laws—not the Union Government.

q: In Sri Lanka’s ethnic composition (18% Tamils), what distinguished the two sub-groups?
o: "Sri Lankan Tamils" (13%) were Tamil natives of the country, while "Indian Tamils" (~5%) had forefathers who came from India as plantation workers during colonial period
Sri Lankan Tamils came from Europe
e: Tamil natives of the country are called Sri Lankan Tamils (13%) concentrated in north/east; the rest whose forefathers came from India as colonial plantation workers are Indian Tamils.

q: Which entity among the following has full Statehood powers under the State List rather than being a Union Territory?
e: Jharkhand is a full-fledged State created in 2000, whereas Chandigarh, Lakshadweep and Delhi are cited in NCERT as Union Territories.

q:
Inspect the statements on the Belgian constitutional model:
1. Equal number of Dutch and French ministers in Central Govt.
2. State Governments are NOT subordinate to Central Govt.
3. Separate Community Government per linguistic group.
4. The 1% German-speaking community was completely excluded from Community Govt.
Which are TRUE?
e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are true; statement 4 is false because German-speaking people also elect their own Community Government.

q: What happens when judges appointed by the executive check the functioning of the executive or laws made by legislatures?
o: Horizontal power sharing operates smoothly through a system of checks and balances
e: This mutual oversight among equal branches is the hallmark of horizontal power sharing and the system of checks and balances.

q: Why did coalition governments after 1990 restrain the Union Government from arbitrarily dismissing State Governments?
o: Because major regional parties became indispensable coalition partners in running the Central Government, compelling respect for State autonomy
e: When no single party won a clear Lok Sabha majority, national parties had to enter alliances with regional parties to govern at the Centre—creating respect for State autonomy.

q: A metro city elects a Mayor, a small town elects a Municipal Chairperson, and a village elects a Sarpanch. Which independent body conducts elections for ALL THREE tiers of local bodies?
e: Created under the 1992 amendment, the independent State Election Commission in each State conducts both panchayat and municipal elections.

q: How does the modern democratic understanding of power sharing reject the older traditional notion of political power?
o: Earlier it was believed all power must reside in one person/group for quick decisions, whereas democracy holds people are the source of all political power and power must be shared among as many citizens as possible
e: For a long time it was believed all power must reside in one person/group for quick decisions, but that changed with democracy: one basic principle of democracy is that people are the source of all political power and due respect must be given to diverse groups.

q: What common philosophy connects India’s 22 Scheduled Languages and special constitutional provisions under Article 371?
o: Strengthening national unity by sensitively accommodating linguistic, cultural, and historical diversity rather than imposing forced uniformity
e: The real success of federalism in India owes not merely to constitutional rules, but to the democratic politics of respecting diversity and the desire for living together.

q: Which statement comparing Federal and Unitary systems is INCORRECT?
o: In a unitary system, either there is only one level of government or sub-units are subordinate to central govt
In a unitary system, the central govt can pass on orders to provincial or local govt
In a federal system, state governments are subordinate agents directly under central command
In a federal system, both levels of government are separately answerable to the people
e: In a federal system, state governments are NOT subordinate to the central government; they possess independent powers of their own.

q: Under the 1992 Constitutional Amendments in India, at which tier of government was at least one-third reservation for women made constitutionally mandatory?
o: In rural and urban local government bodies (Panchayats and Municipalities)
In Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha right from 1992
e: The 1992 amendments mandated at least one-third reservation for women specifically in local self-government bodies (Panchayats and Municipalities).
